messages:
jess (support): Heads up — FinSparks is hitting repeated 429s in EU-prod for the last 30m. Started as small blips but now ~10% of requests are 429. Customer says they didn't change code. sample request-id: rq_0a1b2c3d. stack: mobile -> edge-proxy -> rw-api.
raj (eng-sre): copy. Do we have their RPM/TPM numbers? any spikes in concurrency or bursts from the edge?
jess (support): Customer reports ~600 RPM normally, spiked to ~1.8k over 15m window. They say concurrency didn't change intentionally, but mobile SDK got an update 40m ago (v3.2.1). Eli is looped in with the release notes.
eli (customer-success): I pinged the customer — they said retries are exponential backoff but they increased client threads on a gradual rollout. They also mentioned some background sync jobs that may have kicked in.
raj (eng-sre): OK likely burst -> token-bucket exhaust on the per-customer quota. Can we confirm which rate limit enforced? Mia, can you check the RW gateway logs for x-rate-limit headers and which throttle rule fired? Also check if it was per-api-key or per-organization cap.
mia (eng-runtime): pulling logs. I see repeated 429s from org: finsparks-eu between 1987650200-1987653800. Gateways show enforcement at the edge with rule "org-rpm-v2". Headers we emitted in a handful of responses: `X-RW-RateLimit-Limit: 1200`, `X-RW-RateLimit-Remaining: 0`, `Retry-After: 12`. Most 429s show remaining=0. There are bursts where short-term RPM exceeded 1800 for a 2–3m window.
raj (eng-sre): That matches burst exhaustion. Two angles: 1) client-side reduce retries/concurrency; 2) server-side allowlist or temporary burst allowances. Is the customer on Dedicated or Hosted?
jess (support): Hosted (paid plan but not Dedicated). They asked for a quick mitigation while they roll back client threading.
eli (customer-success): Customer is pushing for a temporary bump or soft-fail config while they revert. What's the policy for short-term bump? Any risk to noisy-neighbor effects?
mia (eng-runtime): We can flip a short-term quota on the org (increase RPM cap from 1200->2200 for 30m) but need SRE signoff — that would reduce 429s immediately but could impact capacity if other orgs surge. Alternatively enable smoother backoff hints by adding `Retry-After` jitter guidance but that doesn't stop immediate 429s.
raj (eng-sre): Before pushing quotas, let's validate reproducible replay and check that requests are not malformed e.g., tight loop of tiny requests. Ask for a sample traffic capture from the customer (first 1k requests around spike). Also check for hot endpoints: embedding vs chat vs token-heavy calls — per-token cost can cause throttle too if system uses TPM.
jess (support): Asked customer for pcap and sample request logs. Also asked them to temporarily reduce client threads to 4 and increase initial backoff to 500ms.
eli (customer-success): Customer started rollout of thread-limiter immediately. They asked whether Redwood exposes per-route metrics in console so they can self-diagnose. I linked docs but they want a pointer.
mia (eng-runtime): Console does show per-route RPM/TPM and quota burn heatmap. I pulled the org heatmap for the window and uploaded screenshot to the private ticket (link: https://redwood.internal/reports/finsparks-eu/spike). Hot endpoints were mostly `/v1/chat/completions` with short prompts (high QPS). Token burn looked normal; it was QPS-driven.
raj (eng-sre): Next: can we reproduce in staging by replaying captured traffic? If it's client-side concurrency causing the spike, a replay at same QPS should trigger the same type of 429s. Mia/eng-runtime — can you spin a temporary replay harness with request pacing preserved? Use the hood-replay tool, target staging gateway with org test key.
mia (eng-runtime): I'll stand up a replay job. Quick tip for support/CS: ask customer to check for retry storm pattern — many clients mis-handle 429 by retrying immediately. Example pattern we saw before:
```
while (!success) {
  send()
  if (status == 429) continue // <-- wrong, immediate retry
}
```
Suggest exponential backoff with jitter, cap retries to 3.
```
# recommended psuedocode
wait = random(0, base) * (2 ** attempt)
```

jess (support): Customer sent a sample chunk (1000 reqs). I uploaded to replay bucket: s3://replay/finsparks/1987654321/sample1.json. They confirmed no malformed headers. Replay in staging with same pacing produced 429s when we ran at ~1.7k RPM. When we slowed to 1.1k RPM, almost zero 429s.
raj (eng-sre): That confirms quota boundary. For mitigation path: short-term options = (A) customer reduces client concurrency/retries (B) we grant temporary burst window (C) recommend batched requests/aggregation. Which does customer prefer?
eli (customer-success): They want (A) immediately and (B) as fallback while they roll back SDK. They asked for guidance on how long to keep quota bump if we do it.
mia (eng-runtime): If we bump quota, keep it short (30–60m) while they roll back. Monitor for cross-org impact. Also suggest they implement exponential backoff + request coalescing on clients.
raj (eng-sre): I'll approve a 30m bump to 2200 RPM for finsparks-eu if eng-runtime can monitor. Mia, can you run the bump and keep an eye on tail latency and capacity? Also add temporary circuit-breaker: if backend CPU > 75% in eu region, revert the bump automatically.
mia (eng-runtime): Running the change now. Patch applied at 1987654400. Monitoring dashboard pinned. oncall-bot: will ping on alert.
oncall-bot: alert subscription enabled for org=finsparks-eu, metric=cpu, threshold=75%, window=2m.
jess (support): I told the customer we're applying a 30m bump and recommended immediate client rollback and backoff changes. They appreciate the quick response.
eli (customer-success): Customer rolled back SDK to v3.2.0 and reduced threads; their 429s dropped to <1% within 8m. They asked for a small docs blurb we can send about "how to avoid rate cap issues" — I drafted a short FAQ entry.
raj (eng-sre): Post-incident follow-ups: 1) update public docs with recommended client retry patterns + SDK best practice, 2) add automated suggestion in Console when an org hits >70% of quota to prompt customers to reduce concurrency or request temporary bump, 3) consider soft-burst allowance for paid-hosted customers with active CS approval.
mia (eng-runtime): Logging note: we should include the org-level burst window length in the `X-RW-RateLimit-*` headers so clients can tune backoff better. Filing a small runtime ticket.
jess (support): Closing loop with customer now. Final status: temporary bump applied and removed after 30m, customer rolled back and issue resolved. Saving thread for postmortem checklist.
eli (customer-success): Nice work all. Saved follow-ups in the ticket. :thumbsup:
